investigation.method: manual review of the live website plus selected local evidence already stored in this repo
investigation.scope_note: This report distinguishes live routes, website claims, legacy routes that still render, and historical evidence from local notes/screenshots.

headline: New Bank's intended appointment front door appears to be PATCHS, but the live site still exposes Silicon Practice forms and Accurx wording. The safer reading is not 'contradictory' in the abstract; it is a multi-layered transition with live legacy routes, current PATCHS messaging, and stale complaints content.

live_stack.label: Public website stack
live_stack.platform: WordPress with nhsuk-frontend-theme and Silicon Practice plugins
evidence: The homepage exposes a WordPress generator tag.

live_stack.label: Legacy/form platform still on the site
live_stack.platform: Silicon Practice hosted forms on newbank.nhs.uk/form/*
evidence: The site still links to local form routes for medical help, nurse/HCA requests, cancellation, test results and contact-the-practice.
Those routes render live forms on the practice domain.

live_stack.label: Current intended online consultation platform
evidence: The homepage banner says that from 1 October all requests made by phone, in person or online go through Patchs Health.
The appointments page links directly to patchs.ai/newbankmedicalpractice/login.
The September 2025 PATCHS FAQ PDF says all appointment requests should go through Patchs Health.

live_stack.label: NHS App wording still visible on the site
evidence: The appointments page tells NHS App users to continue to the accurx system.

current_routes.label: PATCHS direct route
notes: The standalone PATCHS login page is reachable.
The practice website and PATCHS FAQ both present this as the current route for requests.

current_routes.label: Legacy medical-help form on the practice site
notes: This route still renders a local form and is still linked from the medical-help page.
The form asks for callback availability and interpreter needs.
The source also contains capacity and closure notices.

current_routes.label: NHS App route
notes: The site tells patients to use the NHS App and then continue to the accurx system.
This wording conflicts with the same page's PATCHS messaging, so treat it as a route claim rather than a confirmed current integration.

current_routes.label: Phone route
current_routes.kind: staff-assisted intake, not a distinct digital platform
notes: The site says patients can phone the practice.
The PATCHS FAQ says requests by phone still go through Patchs Health.
Do not treat phone as an independent appointment system; it is presented as staff-assisted intake into the same workflow.

current_routes.label: In-person route
current_routes.kind: staff-assisted intake, not a distinct digital platform
notes: The site and PDF say staff can help patients who visit in person.
Again, this is described as support into the same request workflow, not direct walk-up booking.

current_routes.label: Administrative contact form
notes: A separate contact-the-practice form still exists on the site.
The page says it is for non-urgent general enquiries and promises a response within 2 working days.

operational_rules_and_claims.label: PATCHS opening-hours claim
notes: The September 2025 PATCHS FAQ says appointment requests are accessible during practice opening hours.
The same FAQ says administrative queries can be submitted 24/7.

operational_rules_and_claims.label: Callback rule on legacy local form
notes: The local medical-help form says that if a phone call is needed the clinician will try twice, and if both calls are missed the patient must fill in another form.

operational_rules_and_claims.label: Capacity closure notice on legacy local form
notes: The source contains a notice saying medical appointments can close after capacity is reached and patients should use the local walk-in centre or NHS 111.

complaints_and_feedback.headline: The website's complaints area is not current enough to rely on.

items.label: Feedback and complaints page
notes: The page still says GTD will add its own information after taking over on 2025-04-01.
It does not provide a current working complaints process or form.

items.label: Complaints form
notes: No current complaint form or clearly usable current route was identified during this pass.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: PATCHS vs Accurx wording
notes: The appointments page says all requests go through PATCHS but still tells NHS App users to continue to Accurx.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: PATCHS intention vs legacy forms still linked
notes: The website presents PATCHS as the new system but still links directly to live Silicon Practice forms.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: Indefinite 'Form Unavailable' notice in source
notes: The local form source includes an indefinite 'Form Unavailable' notice even though the page still renders a live form.

historical_repo_evidence.path: meetings-notes/2025-11-26-meeting3/rubbish website -  down and offline out of hours/no-out-of-hours-at-all.png
notes: Local screenshot evidence suggests clinical request intake was unavailable out of hours after the PATCHS rollout.
Local notes say admin requests on PATCHS were open out of hours from 2026-01-14, while appointment requests remained the concern.

probably_true: PATCHS is the intended current appointment/request platform.
Silicon Practice routes are still live enough that patients can still encounter them.
Phone and in-person routes are better understood as staff-assisted intake into the same workflow than as separate access systems.
needs_follow_up: Whether the NHS App still really hands New Bank requests to Accurx, or whether the wording is just stale.
Whether the local Silicon Practice forms still submit into a live operational workflow or are legacy routes left hanging on the site.
What the live PATCHS clinical versus admin opening-hours configuration is today, rather than in the September 2025 rollout documents.
